To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a new end-to-end deep learning-based approach to stereo matching that is able to learn the parameters of cost volume smoothing and disparity selection.

(1) end-to-end deep learning of stereo matching can achieve state-of-the-art results, (2) end-to-end training of stereo matching does not require deep learning of image appearance descriptors, (3) end-to-end stereo matching training can be achieved by learning the parameters of cost volume smoothing process, (4) cost volume smoothing can be implemented using differentiable domain-transform, and (5) end-to-end learning of stereo matching is very efficient at test time.

(1) deep learning can successfully be used to learn the parameters of classical cost volume aggregation algorithms; (2) by using differentiable domain transforms, we can train such parameters end-to-end with the rest of the stereo pipeline; (3) this approach is highly efficient and can be used to train stereo matching systems that are fast at test time, and (4) such systems can achieve good matching accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new deep learning architecture that can efficiently and effectively learn to perform stereo matching.

the following question: is it possible to achieve good stereo matching accuracy with a very simple cost volume representation, while using deep learning to learn the optimal cost volume aggregation parameters?

the following questions: How can we use deep learning to speed up stereo matching without sacrificing accuracy? What is the best way to use deep learning for stereo matching? Can we use deep learning for the entire stereo pipeline?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is the best method to date in terms of accuracy vs. speed.
the method presented in this paper is a very promising approach to dense stereo matching that can be used for a wide range of practical applications.
the proposed method is the best performing real-time method on the KITTI benchmark.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of speed and matching accuracy.
our approach is able to match or outperform the best previous approaches in terms of matching accuracy, while running much faster at test time.

we show how to use deep learning to learn the parameters of classical stereo matching algorithms, and in particular, how to use a recurrent neural network to learn the parameters that control the aggregation of cost volumes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the dense stereo setting, deep learning can be successfully used to learn the local parameters of classical algorithms, rather than to learn pixel descriptors.
deep learning can be effectively used not only for learning pixel descriptors, but also for learning the parameters of the classical matching pipeline.

the performance of deep stereo matching methods can be improved without using deep learning of pixel descriptors, and that the performance of classical methods can be improved by learning the parameters of the aggregation process.
